title: How to Choose Hardwood Flooring From Samples: A Method That Works
meta: How to choose hardwood flooring from samples: narrow to three, lay them flat in your own Kirkland light for five days, then decide. Wills Flooring's method.
keywords: how to choose hardwood flooring from samples, hardwood floor samples at home, pick hardwood floor color, hardwood flooring Kirkland WA, engineered hardwood samples, compare hardwood floor samples
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Narrow to three samples before anything touches your floor, lay them flat where the real floor will go, look at them in morning, noon and lamp light for five days, and pick the one you stopped noticing.
blocks.detail: Holding a small chip up to a wall in a showroom is how people end up with a floor that looks orange next to their cabinets. The floor is horizontal, it is huge, and it lives in your light, not the store's. Here is the method we use on every Kirkland estimate.

blocks.html: A common thread on remodel forums goes: "We loved the sample, hated the floor." It is almost never the product's fault. A 4 by 6 inch chip under warm showroom spotlights tells you nothing about how 1,100 sq ft of it reads in a Houghton living room facing the lake, or in a Finn Hill house where tall firs keep the main floor in shade until noon. Kirkland buyers also judge floors hard at resale. This is a process, and it takes about a week.

blocks.text: Step one: make four decisions before you look at a single board

items.title: Species and grade
items.text: White oak, red oak, maple, hickory or walnut. Then the grade: select (clean, even) or character (knots, mineral streaks). Pick this by how much variation you can live with. A character sample with two knots may become a floor with two hundred.

items.title: Width and length
items.text: Narrow 2 1/4 in strip reads traditional and busy; 5 to 7 in plank reads current and calm. Longer boards make a room look bigger. Decide this from your room size, not from the sample, which is always short.

items.title: Color family
items.text: Natural, light, mid-brown or dark. Kirkland's gray winter light pushes cool colors flat and warm colors muddy, so most of our Eastside customers end up in natural or light with a neutral undertone.

items.title: Finish sheen and texture
items.text: Matte or satin hides dust and scratches. Smooth, wire-brushed or hand-scraped changes how light bounces. Decide matte vs satin now, because a glossy sample will win in a showroom and lose in your kitchen.

blocks.note: With these four settled, we pull three finalists from Metropolitan Hardwood and other lines and bring them to your house.

items.text: Lay all three flat on the actual floor, in the room with the most light and the room with the least. Not against the wall, not on the counter. Put them a foot apart so the eye compares fairly.

Look at 8 am, 1 pm and after dark with only your normal lamps on. Take a phone photo each time from standing height. Kirkland's south-facing lakefront rooms can shift a color two shades between noon and dusk.

Set a cabinet door, a baseboard offcut, a paint swatch and a leg of your sofa next to each sample. The floor has to get along with all of them. Watch for orange or pink undertones fighting a gray cabinet.

Drag a key across the back corner, set a wet glass on it for an hour, walk on it in dirty shoes. You are checking how scratches and water spots show, not whether the wood is tough. Light matte finishes forgive the most.

Remove the one you keep noticing for the wrong reason. Of the two left, pick the one that made every photo look calmer. If you cannot choose, the safer one for resale in Kirkland is the lighter, more neutral board.

blocks.note: Labor only at Wills Flooring's published rates. The material you chose from the samples, plus underlayment, removal and any subfloor prep, is quoted at the free estimate.

blocks.text: What to look at on the sample itself

head: Look at
How
What it tells you
rows: Check the edge; measure the top veneer
Under 2 mm cannot be sanded later; 3 mm and up can be refinished once or twice.
Count the plies on the edge
Multi-ply birch or a dense HDF core stays flatter through Kirkland's wet winters than a thin 3-ply.
Run a finger across the joint
Micro-bevels hide unevenness but collect dirt; square edges look seamless but need a flatter subfloor.
Aluminum-oxide factory finishes are the most scratch-resistant. Oil finishes look richer and need re-oiling.
Ask for two boards, not one
One board is a single tree. Two boards show the spread you will actually get across a room.
blocks.note: Ask for full-length boards or a 12 by 12 in panel when you can. Two 4 in chips is a guess, not a sample.

blocks.title: A Kirkland-specific warning:
blocks.text: Lakefront and view homes in Houghton and Juanita get intense low-angle afternoon light. Dark and high-gloss samples look stunning in it for one hour and show every footprint the other twenty-three. If the room has a west window over the water, weight your day-two evening photo heavily.
Sample mistakes that lead to regret

items.html: Choosing from a photo or a website swatch. Screens add saturation and cannot show sheen. Never order a floor you have not seen flat in your own house.
Matching the floor to the furniture you have now. Sofas change every eight years. Match the floor to the fixed things: cabinets, trim color, stair treads, fireplace stone.
Judging a character-grade floor from a clean board. Ask to see the ugliest board in the carton. If you can live with that one, you can live with the floor.
Ignoring what the next buyer sees. Kirkland resale expectations are high. A trend color that will read dated in six years costs you at sale time even if you love it today.
Your three finalists and your phone photos. We will tell you which one we have seen age well in Eastside homes and which one we would not install over your particular subfloor.

The rough square footage and stair count. A 1,100 sq ft Rose Hill main floor with 14 stairs is 1,100 × $3.25 + 14 × $125 = $5,325 in labor at our published rates; material is added after you pick the board.
A cabinet door and a trim offcut. We compare them to the boards on the spot. If you are also weighing engineered vs solid, read our Kirkland comparison first.

Questions about the subfloor. Many 1970s to 90s Kirkland homes have particleboard under carpet, which cannot take nails. It changes the install method, and you should know before you fall for a solid 3/4 in plank.
The warranty you expect. Wills Flooring backs hardwood installation with a 1-year workmanship warranty; the manufacturer covers the finish. Get both in writing.

faq.q: How many hardwood samples should I take home?
faq.a: Three. More than that and the differences blur and you default to the safest choice. Do the narrowing on paper first: species, width, color family and sheen. Then ask for three boards that fit those four answers and compare only those.

faq.q: How big should a hardwood flooring sample be?
faq.a: As big as you can get. Two full boards or a 12 by 12 inch panel shows grain, color spread and bevel. A 4 inch chip shows one spot on one tree. Our mobile showroom brings large boards to Kirkland homes for this reason.

faq.q: Why does my hardwood sample look different at home than in the store?
faq.a: Store lighting is warm, bright and comes from above. Your home has side daylight that changes through the day and mixes with lamps at night. Wood also reads darker flat on the floor than held at eye level. Always judge samples flat, at home.

faq.q: Should I match hardwood to my kitchen cabinets?
faq.a: Coordinate, do not match. A floor the same tone as the cabinets makes the kitchen disappear into itself. Aim for a floor one or two steps lighter or darker with a compatible undertone, and check it against the countertop edge too.

faq.q: What if I like the sample but want a different color?
faq.a: Choose unfinished hardwood and have it stained on site. Wills installs unfinished at $2.75 per sq ft, then sands, stains and finishes at our refinishing rates. Ask for a stained test board on your actual species before the floor goes in.

faq.q: Can Wills Flooring bring hardwood samples to my house in Kirkland?
faq.a: Yes. That is what the mobile showroom does. We bring boards in the species and colors you narrowed to, measure the rooms, check the subfloor and leave a firm written quote. The samples can stay for your five-day test.
